The industry is asking the wrong question about Devin, Copilot, and AI software engineers.  The question isn't: "Can an LLM write code?" (Any 7B model can spit out Python syntax). The real question is: "Can an autonomous AI survive in an enterprise monorepo without breaking production?"  In 2026, 87% of autonomous coding loops fail because of three fatal architectural flaws:  1. The Wrapper Hallucination: Agents write code directly against raw chat prompts. They hallucinate packages that don't exist, modify unstaged files, and push breaking changes without containment.  2. Zero Worktree State Isolation: Real engineering requires ephemeral Git Worktrees. If an AI agent isn't isolated in a dedicated sandbox worktree with strict process boundaries, it corrupts repo state.  3. The Missing Pre-Commit Forensic Gate: In enterprise software, an agent's work cannot be trusted on "faith". Every patch must pass AST syntax interrogation, clean local compilation (exit code 0), and cryptographically verified SHA-256 state tracking before human signoff.  Chatbots give you code suggestions.
